# STR Scanner v3 False Positive Analysis
## Rally Forge Service Treatment Record Extraction Issues
**Date:** March 26, 2026
**Severity:** High â€” Metadata/context being misclassified as medical conditions
**Affected Component:** STR Scanner v3.1 (Backend va_scanner subsystem)
---
## Executive Summary
The STR scanner is extracting **document metadata, provider information, and geographic context as if they were actual service-connected conditions**. This creates false positives in four primary areas:
1. **Geographic Location Confusion** â€” "Afghanistan" appears as a condition instead of deployment context
2. **Provider Name Extraction** â€” "Fletcher" (doctor name) extracted as condition reference
3. **Document Header Matching** â€” "LOD Event" from document headers marked as LOD status
4. **AHLTA Reference Contamination** â€” Document format indicators appearing in conditions field
The root cause is **insufficient context filtering and lack of metadata/header exclusion patterns** in the extraction library.

## Issue Details
### Issue 1: Geographic Locations Extracted as Deployment Indicators
**Location:** [extractionLibrary.js](backend/va_scanner/backend/shared/scanner/strAnalysis/extractionLibrary.js#L698) â€” `extractDeploymentIndicators()` function
**Problem Code:**
```javascript
// Lines 693â€“707
const DEPLOYMENT_PATTERNS = [
  /\b(pre-?deployment\s+(?:health\s+)?assessment|ptha)\b/i,
  /\b(post-?deployment\s+(?:health\s+)?assessment|pdha|pdhra)\b/i,
  /\b(exposure\s+questionnaire)\b/i,
  /\b(combat[\s-]related)\b/i,
  /\b(deployed|deployment)\b/i,
  /\b(oif|oef|ond|operation\s+(?:iraqi|enduring|new\s+dawn|freedom))\b/i,
  /\b(iraq|afghanistan|kuwait|somalia|kosovo|syria|vietnam|korea|persian\s+gulf)\b/i,  // â† PROBLEM
];
const THEATER_PATTERNS = /\b(iraq|afghanistan|kuwait|persian\s+gulf|vietnam|korea|southwest\s+asia|gulf\s+war|pacific)\b/i;
```
**Impact:**
- **"Afghanistan"** appears in document headers or location references (e.g., "Treated in Afghanistan military facility") â†’ extracted as `theaterOfOperations: "Afghanistan"`
- **"Guam"** (not in current pattern but similar issue) â†’ would extract as deployment location
- **"Kuwait"** in office addresses â†’ extracted as military deployment reference
- No distinction between **"deployed to Afghanistan"** (actual deployment) vs. **"Document prepared in Afghanistan"** (metadata/context)
**Root Cause:**
- Patterns match **ANY occurrence** of location keywords
- No context analysis (e.g., checking for "deployed to", "sent to", "stationed in", etc.)
- No exclusion of lines containing document metadata keywords (e.g., "Received:", "Dated:", "Facility Location:")
**False Positive Example:**
```
RAW TEXT:  "C&P Exam | Location: Kabul, Afghanistan | Date: 2024-01-15"
EXTRACTED: { indicatorType: "deployment reference", theaterOfOperations: "Afghanistan", ... }
EXPECTED:  Should be tagged as metadata, not deployment
```
---
### Issue 2: Provider Names Extracted as Condition References
**Location:** [extractionLibrary.js](backend/va_scanner/backend/shared/scanner/strAnalysis/extractionLibrary.js#L260â€“280) â€” Multiple extraction functions
**Problem:**
The scanner has **no mechanism to exclude provider names** from extracted conditions. Example:
- Line contains: `"Seen by: MAJ Fletcher, MD (Neurology)"`
- Provider type correctly identified: `providerType: "neurology"`
- **BUT** "Fletcher" can appear in other lines without provider context and be extracted as a reference
**Root Cause:**
- No provider name blocklist or exclusion pattern
- No facility/location filtering before extraction
- No check for "common proper names" that shouldn't be conditions
**False Positive Example:**
```
RAW TEXT: "Patient reports seeing Dr. Fletcher for specialized evaluation"
EXTRACTED: { ???: "Fletcher" } in some contexts
EXPECTED:  Should filter "Fletcher" as provider name, not extract as condition
```
---
### Issue 3: Document Header LOD References Mistaken for Status
**Location:** [extractionLibrary.js](backend/va_scanner/backend/shared/scanner/strAnalysis/extractionLibrary.js#L628â€“665) â€” `extractProfilesAndDutyLimits()` function
**Problem Code:**
```javascript
// Lines 628â€“630
const LOD_IN_PATTERN = /\b(?:in\s+line\s+of\s+duty|ild|in\s+lod)\b/i;
const LOD_NOT_PATTERN = /\b(?:not\s+in\s+line\s+of\s+duty|nild|not\s+in\s+lod)\b/i;

if (!hasProfile && !hasLOD) return;
```
**Impact:**
- Document header line: `"--- LOD Event History ---"` â†’ matches `hasLOD`
- Line is extracted with unclear `lodStatus: null`
- Cross-validation cannot distinguish between:
  - Actual LOD assertion: `"Injury determined to be in line of duty"`
  - Document section header: `"LOD Event Header"`
  - Abbreviation in text: `"The LOD event occurred..."`
**False Positive Example:**
```
RAW TEXT: "*** LOD Event Summary Report ***"
EXTRACTED: { profileType: null, lodStatus: null, rawText: "*** LOD Event Summary Report ***" }
EXPECTED:  Should be excluded as document metadata, not extracted as a profile
```
---
### Issue 4: AHLTA References in Conditions Field
**Location:** [extractionLibrary.js](backend/va_scanner/backend/shared/scanner/strAnalysis/extractionLibrary.js) â€” Multiple extraction functions
**Problem:**
- AHLTA (Armed Forces Health Longitudinal Technology Application) document markers appear in text
- Example: `"AHLTA Record: 12345"` or `"AHLTA Note"`
- These should be **metadata context**, not extracted as conditions
**Root Cause:**
- No metadata keyword exclusion list
- No filtering for system/document format references
- Event patterns too broad and don't check context
**False Positive Example:**
```
RAW TEXT: "AHLTA Reference: ICD-10 Code Assignment"
EXTRACTED: Potential event extraction depending on pattern match
EXPECTED:  Should be excluded as document metadata
```

```

    â”œâ”€ extractEvents()

    â”œâ”€ extractProfilesAndDutyLimits() â† ISSUE #3 (LOD header matching)
    â”œâ”€ extractMentalHealthIndicators()
    â””â”€ [other extraction functions]
    â†“
buildStrAnalysis() [strAnalysis/index.js]
    â”œâ”€ All extraction functions called again  â† NO FILTERING HERE
    â”œâ”€ buildConditionPatterns()
    â”œâ”€ buildConditionTimelines()
    â””â”€ runCrossValidation() [crossValidation.js]  â† Should catch false positives but doesn't
    â†“
validateSTRSchema() [schemaValidators.js]  â† Validates structure, not semantic truth
    â†“

```
**Key Gap:** No **post-extraction metadata filtering** or **context validation** step occurs.
---
## Proposed Fix Approach
### Strategy: Multi-Layer Filtering
**Layer 1: Exclude Document Metadata Keywords**
- Create blacklist/exclusion patterns for common document headers and metadata
- Example: `"LOD Event"`, `"AHLTA Reference"`, `"Location:"`, `"Facility:"`, etc.
**Layer 2: Context-Aware Pattern Matching**
- Modify patterns to require deployment context (e.g., "deployed to" + location)
- Add negative lookahead patterns to exclude isolated location mentions
**Layer 3: Provider Name Exclusion**
- Create provider name blocklist (common military provider names, doctors' names)
- Filter provider names from extraction outputs
**Layer 4: Cross-Validation Enhancement**
- Add cross-validation checks to flag extracted items that appear only in headers/metadata
- Add confidence scoring based on line context
---
## Recommended Fixes
### Fix 1: Add Metadata Exclusion Filters
**File:** [extractionLibrary.js](backend/va_scanner/backend/shared/scanner/strAnalysis/extractionLibrary.js)
**Action:** Add helper function and apply before extraction:
```javascript
// NEW: Add near top of file (around line 65)
// Metadata keywords that indicate document headers/structure, not medical content
const METADATA_KEYWORDS = [
  'lod event',      // Document section header
  'ahlta',          // System reference
  'location:',      // Address/facility location
  'facility:',      // MTF name
  'received:',      // Document date
  'dated:',         // Document date
  'from:',          // Sender
  'to:',            // Recipient
  'page',           // Page reference
  'section',        // Document section
  'exhibit',        // Exhibit reference
  'report type:',   // Form type
  'chart#',         // Chart number
  'dod id',         // Identifier
];
// NEW: Helper function to detect metadata lines
export function isLikelyMetadataLine(line) {
  if (!line || typeof line !== 'string') return false;
  const lower = line.toLowerCase();
  // Check for metadata keywords
  if (METADATA_KEYWORDS.some(keyword => lower.includes(keyword))) {
    return true;
  }
  // Check for typical document header patterns
  if (/^[\*\-=_]{3,}/.test(line)) return true;  // Separator lines
  if (/^\d+\s*[a-z]\.\s+/.test(line)) return true;  // Block numbering (e.g., "1a. ")
  if (/^[A-Z ]{5,}:?\s*$/.test(line)) return true;  // All-caps headers
  return false;
}
```
**Action:** Update extraction functions to skip metadata lines:
```javascript
// MODIFIED: extractProfilesAndDutyLimits (around line 645)
export function extractProfilesAndDutyLimits(lines) {
  const profiles = [];
  const seen = new Set();
  lines.forEach((line, idx) => {
    // NEW: Skip metadata lines
    if (isLikelyMetadataLine(line)) return;
    const hasProfile = /\b(profile|duty\s+limitation|limited\s+duty|light\s+duty|physical\s+profile|fitness\s+for\s+duty)\b/i.test(line);
    const hasLOD = /\b(lod|line\s+of\s+duty)\b/i.test(line);
    if (!hasProfile && !hasLOD) return;
    // ... rest of function
  });
  return profiles;
}
```

### Fix 2: Context-Aware Deployment Pattern Matching
**File:** [extractionLibrary.js](backend/va_scanner/backend/shared/scanner/strAnalysis/extractionLibrary.js)
**Action:** Refactor `extractDeploymentIndicators()` to require deployment context:
```javascript
// MODIFIED: Lines 693â€“750
const DEPLOYMENT_ASSERTION_PATTERNS = [
  /\b(pre-?deployment\s+(?:health\s+)?assessment|ptha)\b/i,
  /\b(post-?deployment\s+(?:health\s+)?assessment|pdha|pdhra)\b/i,
  /\b(exposure\s+questionnaire)\b/i,
  /\bdeployed\s+(?:to\s+)?(?:iraq|afghanistan|kuwait|somalia|kosovo|syria|vietnam|korea|persian\s+gulf)\b/i,
  /\bstationed\s+(?:in\s+)?(?:iraq|afghanistan|kuwait|somalia|kosovo|syria|vietnam|korea|persian\s+gulf)\b/i,
  /\bsent\s+(?:to\s+)?(?:iraq|afghanistan|kuwait|somalia|kosovo|syria|vietnam|korea|persian\s+gulf)\b/i,
  /\b(combat[\s-]related)\b/i,
  /\b(oif|oef|ond|operation\s+(?:iraqi|enduring|new\s+dawn|freedom))\b/i,
];
// NEW: Patterns for location mentions in context (not deployment)
const LOCATION_CONTEXT_PATTERNS = [
  /\blocation\s*:\s*/i,           // "Location: "
  /\bfacility\s*:\s*/i,           // "Facility: "
  /\b(?:mtf|vamc)\s*:\s*/i,       // "MTF: " / "VAMC: "
  /\baddress\s*:\s*/i,            // "Address: "
  /\b(?:from|to)\s+\w+\s+\w+,?\s+(?:iraq|afghanistan|kuwait|somalia|kosovo|syria|vietnam|korea|[a-z]+\s+gulf)\b/i,  // Address lines
];
export function extractDeploymentIndicators(lines) {
  const indicators = [];
  const seen = new Set();
  lines.forEach((line, idx) => {
    // NEW: Skip metadata lines
    if (isLikelyMetadataLine(line)) return;
    // NEW: Check if line is just a location context mention (not deployment)
    if (LOCATION_CONTEXT_PATTERNS.some(p => p.test(line))) {
      return;  // Skip location metadata, not deployment indicator
    }
    const date = parseDateFromText(line);
    const lineNumber = idx + 1;
    for (const pattern of DEPLOYMENT_ASSERTION_PATTERNS) {
      if (!pattern.test(line)) continue;
      const key = `dep|${line.slice(0, 60)}`.toLowerCase();
      if (seen.has(key)) break;
      seen.add(key);
      const theaterMatch = line.match(/(?:iraq|afghanistan|kuwait|somalia|kosovo|syria|vietnam|korea|persian\s+gulf)/i);
      indicators.push({
        id: generateId('dep'),
        indicatorType: classifyDeploymentType(line),
        theaterOfOperations: theaterMatch ? theaterMatch[0] : null,
        exposureStatement: line.trim(),
        date,
        rawText: line,
        lineNumber,
        confidence: calculateDeploymentConfidence(line),  // NEW
      });
      break;
    }
  });
  return indicators;
}
// NEW: Helper to score deployment confidence
function calculateDeploymentConfidence(line) {
  const lower = line.toLowerCase();
  if (/\bdeployed\s+(?:to|in)/.test(lower)) return 0.95;
  if (/\bstationed\s+(?:in|at)/.test(lower)) return 0.90;
  if (/\b(?:oif|oef|ond)\b/.test(lower)) return 0.90;
  return 0.70;  // Generic deployment reference
}
```

### Fix 3: Provider Name Exclusion
**File:** [extractionLibrary.js](backend/va_scanner/backend/shared/scanner/strAnalysis/extractionLibrary.js)
**Action:** Add provider name filtering:
```javascript
// NEW: Provider name/title keywords to exclude (around line 70)
const PROVIDER_NAME_INDICATORS = [
  /\b(?:dr\.|doctor|physician|md|do|rn|np|pa|lt\.?\s*col|maj|capt|sgt|cpl|col)\s+([A-Z][a-z]+)\b/i,
  /\bprovider\s*:\s*([A-Z][a-z]+)/i,
  /\breferred\s+by\s*:\s*([A-Z][a-z]+)/i,
];
// NEW: Common military provider names (expandable)
const COMMON_PROVIDER_NAMES = new Set([
  'fletcher', 'smith', 'johnson', 'williams', 'jones', 'brown', 'davis', 'miller',
  // Add more as needed
]);
// NEW: Helper to check if text is likely a provider name mention
export function isProviderNameContext(line) {
  for (const pattern of PROVIDER_NAME_INDICATORS) {
    if (pattern.test(line)) return true;
  }
  return false;
}
// NEW: Extract provider names from line to exclude them
export function extractProviderNamesToExclude(line) {
  const names = new Set();
  const patterns = [
    /\b(?:dr\.|doctor)\s+([A-Z][a-z]+)\b/i,
    /\b(?:seen\s+by|examined\s+by|evaluated\s+by)\s*:\s*([A-Z][a-z]+)/i,
  ];
  for (const pattern of patterns) {
    const m = line.match(pattern);
    if (m && m[1]) {
      names.add(m[1].toLowerCase());
    }
  }
  return names;
}
```

### Fix 4: Enhanced Cross-Validation
**File:** [crossValidation.js](backend/va_scanner/backend/shared/scanner/strAnalysis/crossValidation.js)
**Action:** Add metadata-based false positive detection:
```javascript
// NEW: Add function to detect metadata-derived false positives (around line 100)
export function detectMetadataDerivedFalsePositives(strAnalysis) {
  const flags = [];
  // Check deployment indicators that appear only in lines with location context patterns
  for (const indicator of strAnalysis.deploymentIndicators || []) {
    const line = indicator.rawText || '';
    if (/\b(?:location|facility|address)\s*[:=]/.test(line.toLowerCase())) {
      flags.push({
        type: 'metadataDerivedFalsePositive',
        category: 'deploymentIndicator',
        description: 'Deployment indicator extracted from location metadata line',
        lineNumber: indicator.lineNumber,
        rawText: line,
        extractedValue: indicator.theaterOfOperations,
        recommendation: 'Review - likely metadata, not actual deployment',
        confidence: 'high',
      });
    }
  }
  // Check LOD indicators in header lines
  for (const profile of strAnalysis.profilesAndDutyLimits || []) {
    const line = (profile.rawText || '').toLowerCase();
    if (/^[\*\-=]{3,}|lod\s+event|report\s+header/.test(line)) {
      flags.push({
        type: 'metadataDerivedFalsePositive',
        category: 'profileOrDutyLimit',
        description: 'Profile/LOD extracted from document header line',
        lineNumber: profile.lineNumber,
        rawText: profile.rawText,
        recommendation: 'Review - likely section header, not actual duty limitation',
        confidence: 'high',
      });
    }
  }
  return flags;
}
```
**Action:** Update `runCrossValidation()` to include new check:

```javascript
export function runCrossValidation(strAnalysis) {
  return [
    ...detectRecurringPatterns(strAnalysis),
    ...detectMedicationsWithoutDiagnoses(strAnalysis),
    ...detectTestsWithoutLinkedConditions(strAnalysis),
    ...detectFunctionalImpactWithoutLinkedConditions(strAnalysis),
    ...detectTreatmentGaps(strAnalysis),

  ];
}
```

# Rally Forge Copilot Instructions (Canonical)
This file is the canonical instruction source for repository-scoped Copilot behavior.
## Purpose
Assist with development, modernization, documentation, and expansion of Rally Forge in a deterministic, safe, auditable, and non-destructive way.
## Instruction Precedence
1. System and platform safety/policy requirements.
2. Explicit user request in the current task.
3. Repository instructions in this file.
If a user request conflicts with safety, policy, legal, or security requirements, follow higher-priority requirements and provide a safe alternative.
## Absolute Rules
- Do not rewrite, delete, or refactor files unless explicitly requested.
- Do not invent APIs, schemas, endpoints, data fields, or folder structures.
- Do not assume missing context when a clarification is required.
- Do not generate hidden-state or ambiguous behavior.
## Required Behavior
- Use modular, domain-driven patterns.
- Prefer explicit imports, explicit typing where applicable, and explicit return behavior.
- Prefer small, composable functions over large blocks.
- Keep output deterministic and reversible.
- Keep output implementation-ready and aligned to Rally Forge architecture.
## Repository Scope
Assume repository root is the current workspace root and route changes to the proper domain area:
- Frontend
- Backend
- Database
- UX
- UI
- Architecture
- Documentation
- Schemas
- Engines
- Workflows
- Testing
- Deployment
- Governance
- Compliance
- Branding
- Accessibility
- Developer Onboarding
## API Integration Rules
- Use documented/approved endpoints only.
- Use service-layer abstractions for external integrations.
- Avoid calling external APIs directly from UI components.
- Normalize responses into schema-aligned objects.
- Include error handling, retries when appropriate, and logging.
- Never expose secrets, keys, or credentials.
API priority tiers:
- Tier 1: VA Benefits, VA Claims, VA Verification, SkillBridge
- Tier 2: Financial APIs (CFPB, COLI, IRS)
- Tier 3: Community and support APIs
## Schema Rules
- Prefer JSON Schema Draft 2020-12 for new JSON schemas.
- Include `$id`, `type`, `required`, and `properties` where applicable.
- Include representative examples when useful.
- Keep naming consistent with existing repository conventions.
## Engine Rules
- Prefer pure functions for domain engine logic.
- Avoid side effects and hidden external state in engine units.
- Enforce deterministic input-to-output behavior.
- Include validation and explicit error paths.
## Documentation Rules
- Use Markdown for docs updates.
- Include purpose, inputs, outputs, examples, and edge cases as relevant.
- Include upgrade guidance when relevant.
- Do not contradict established docs without calling out the change.
- Follow `MD_Files` structure where applicable.
## Modernization Guidance Rules
When asked for modernization recommendations:
- Use scan evidence from the repository.
- Provide deterministic and heuristic recommendations.
- Label severity as Info, Warning, or Critical.
- Provide concrete next actions, not vague guidance.
- Align recommendations with architecture and modernization roadmap artifacts.
## Working Modes
- Scan mode: identify gaps, inconsistencies, missing components.
- Recommendation mode: prioritized improvements with rationale.
- Architecture mode: modular system-level designs and flows.
- API mode: integration patterns and secure service wrappers.
- Modernization mode: incremental, low-risk upgrade path.
## Communication Expectations
- Be concise, structured, and technical.
- Avoid generic advice.
- Ask clarifying questions only when needed to prevent incorrect action.
- Provide rationale for recommendations.
## Output Expectations
- Deterministic and actionable.
- Ready to apply with minimal rework.
- Clearly structured with headings/lists/code blocks as needed.
- Consistent with Rally Forge architecture and folder conventions.

# @vitejs/plugin-react [![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@vitejs/plugin-react.svg)](https://npmjs.com/package/@vitejs/plugin-react)
The default Vite plugin for React projects.
- enable [Fast Refresh](https://www.npmjs.com/package/react-refresh) in development (requires react >= 16.9)
- use the [automatic JSX runtime](https://legacy.reactjs.org/blog/2020/09/22/introducing-the-new-jsx-transform.html)
- use custom Babel plugins/presets
- small installation size
```js
// vite.config.js
import { defineConfig } from 'vite'
import react from '@vitejs/plugin-react'
export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [react()],
})
```
## Options
### include/exclude
Includes `.js`, `.jsx`, `.ts` & `.tsx` by default. This option can be used to add fast refresh to `.mdx` files:
```js
import { defineConfig } from 'vite'
import react from '@vitejs/plugin-react'
import mdx from '@mdx-js/rollup'
export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [
    { enforce: 'pre', ...mdx() },
    react({ include: /\.(mdx|js|jsx|ts|tsx)$/ }),
  ],
})
```
> `node_modules` are never processed by this plugin (but esbuild will)
### jsxImportSource
Control where the JSX factory is imported from. Default to `'react'`
```js
react({ jsxImportSource: '@emotion/react' })
```
### jsxRuntime
By default, the plugin uses the [automatic JSX runtime](https://legacy.reactjs.org/blog/2020/09/22/introducing-the-new-jsx-transform.html). However, if you encounter any issues, you may opt out using the `jsxRuntime` option.
```js
react({ jsxRuntime: 'classic' })
```
### babel
The `babel` option lets you add plugins, presets, and [other configuration](https://babeljs.io/docs/en/options) to the Babel transformation performed on each included file.
```js
react({
  babel: {
    presets: [...],
    // Your plugins run before any built-in transform (eg: Fast Refresh)
    plugins: [...],
    // Use .babelrc files
    babelrc: true,
    // Use babel.config.js files
    configFile: true,
  }
})
```
Note: When not using plugins, only esbuild is used for production builds, resulting in faster builds.
#### Proposed syntax
If you are using ES syntax that are still in proposal status (e.g. class properties), you can selectively enable them with the `babel.parserOpts.plugins` option:
```js
react({
  babel: {
    parserOpts: {
      plugins: ['decorators-legacy'],
    },
  },
})
```
This option does not enable _code transformation_. That is handled by esbuild.
**Note:** TypeScript syntax is handled automatically.
Here's the [complete list of Babel parser plugins](https://babeljs.io/docs/en/babel-parser#ecmascript-proposalshttpsgithubcombabelproposals).
### reactRefreshHost
The `reactRefreshHost` option is only necessary in a module federation context. It enables HMR to work between a remote & host application. In your remote Vite config, you would add your host origin:
```js
react({ reactRefreshHost: 'http://localhost:3000' })
```
Under the hood, this simply updates the React Fash Refresh runtime URL from `/@react-refresh` to `http://localhost:3000/@react-refresh` to ensure there is only one Refresh runtime across the whole application. Note that if you define `base` option in the host application, you need to include it in the option, like: `http://localhost:3000/{base}`.
## Middleware mode
In [middleware mode](https://vite.dev/config/server-options.html#server-middlewaremode), you should make sure your entry `index.html` file is transformed by Vite. Here's an example for an Express server:
```js
app.get('/', async (req, res, next) => {
  try {
    let html = fs.readFileSync(path.resolve(root, 'index.html'), 'utf-8')
    // Transform HTML using Vite plugins.
    html = await viteServer.transformIndexHtml(req.url, html)
    res.send(html)
  } catch (e) {
    return next(e)
  }
})
```
Otherwise, you'll probably get this error:
```
Uncaught Error: @vitejs/plugin-react can't detect preamble. Something is wrong.
```
### disableOxcRecommendation
If set, disables the recommendation to use `@vitejs/plugin-react-oxc` (which is shown when `rolldown-vite` is detected and `babel` is not configured).
## Consistent components exports
For React refresh to work correctly, your file should only export React components. You can find a good explanation in the [Gatsby docs](https://www.gatsbyjs.com/docs/reference/local-development/fast-refresh/#how-it-works).
If an incompatible change in exports is found, the module will be invalidated and HMR will propagate. To make it easier to export simple constants alongside your component, the module is only invalidated when their value changes.
You can catch mistakes and get more detailed warning with this [eslint rule](https://github.com/ArnaudBarre/eslint-plugin-react-refresh).

# react-refresh
This package implements the wiring necessary to integrate Fast Refresh into bundlers. Fast Refresh is a feature that lets you edit React components in a running application without losing their state. It is similar to an old feature known as "hot reloading", but Fast Refresh is more reliable and officially supported by React.
This package is primarily aimed at developers of bundler plugins. If youâ€™re working on one, here is a [rough guide](https://github.com/facebook/react/issues/16604#issuecomment-528663101) for Fast Refresh integration using this package.

# Constants
Centralized constant values for UI, state, and engine integration.
Rules:
- Keep constants deterministic.
- Do not place business logic in this directory.
- Share stable labels, thresholds, and enum-like values here when reused across modules.

# CI/CD Test Pipeline
## Trigger Policy
- Runs on every commit through push events on all branches.
- Runs on every pull request.
- Runs on merged changes because merges create push events on target branches.
## Pipeline Stages
1. Install and Bootstrap
- Install dependencies.
- Validate environment.
- Validate schema files.
2. Lint and Static Analysis
- Run linter.
- Run type checker.
- Run schema validator.
- Fail on unused imports, dead code, and TODO markers.
3. Unit Tests
- Run all tab-level tests.
- Run all engine-level tests.
- Run all normalization tests.
- Run all mapping table tests.
4. Integration Tests
- Test cross-tab data flow.
- Test silent update triggers.
- Test unified dataset updates.
- Test engine recompute behavior.
5. End-to-End Tests
- Simulate full workflow Profile to Claim Generator.
- Validate final condition list.
- Validate lay statement.
- Validate evidence index.
- Validate timeline.
6. File-Level Audit
- Validate file structure.
- Validate schema imports.
- Validate engine integration.
- Validate no deprecated logic.
7. Build and Package
- Build production bundle.
- Validate build artifacts.
8. Deployment Gate
- Block deployment unless all tests pass.
- Block deployment on warnings.

# CI Quality Ratchet Policy
## Goal
Restore full-repository strict quality gates without reintroducing pipeline instability.
## Rules
- No phase expansion is allowed unless the prior phase is stable for 5 consecutive runs on `main`.
- Warning and violation counts must not increase above the approved baseline.
- Any newly created or modified file is held to strict standards immediately.
## Phases
1. Phase 0 (current): active modernization surfaces only.
2. Phase 1: expand to `backend/controllers` and `backend/services`.
3. Phase 2: expand to scanner backend routes and services.
4. Phase 3: expand to scanner engine and scanner frontend utility layers.
5. Phase 4: expand to `tooling/scripts`.
6. Phase 5: full-repository strict mode with warnings treated as CI failures.
## Metrics Tracked Per Phase
- Lint error count
- Lint warning count
- Static guard violation count
- File-audit violation count
- Deployment-gate pass rate
## Promotion Criteria
- 5 consecutive green runs on `main`.
- No increase in tracked quality metrics.
- No new policy exceptions introduced.
## Rollback Trigger
- Any 2 failures in 3 consecutive `main` runs after a phase expansion.
## Ownership
- Each phase must have one explicit owner and target date.
- Phase transitions require owner sign-off in the tracking issue.

# CI Scope Adjustment Note (2026-03-21)
## Context
- The deployment gate is passing again after CI stabilization work.
- Strict quality checks were narrowed to active modernization surfaces to unblock deterministic delivery.
## What Was Narrowed
- `ci:lint` now runs in error-only mode for CI (`--quiet`).
- `ci:static` scope is focused on active frontend and core backend endpoint/controller surfaces.
- `ci:file-audit` scope is focused on active modernization surfaces.
## Why
- Legacy scanner and tooling trees currently contain large inherited quality debt that caused repeated non-actionable full-repo gate failures.
- The immediate objective was to restore a reliable, deterministic CI signal for active development surfaces.
## Risk
- Some legacy paths are temporarily outside hard-fail CI policy enforcement.
## Mitigation
- A ratchet plan defines phased expansion back to full strict coverage.
- A baseline non-regression guard blocks metric regressions while cleanup proceeds.
## Exit Criteria
- Full-repo strict mode is restored.
- Warnings and policy violations are reduced to zero (or agreed hard threshold) across all in-scope paths.
- The deployment gate remains stable across consecutive main-branch runs.

# Claims Generator: Architectural Redesign (100x Improvement Plan)
**Status**: In Progress
**Target**: Top-tier enterprise architecture with clear separation of concerns
**Impact**: 100x improvement in maintainability, testability, and extensibility
---
## Executive Summary
The current claims generator architecture is **ad-hoc and tightly coupled**. This document outlines a comprehensive restructuring to achieve enterprise-grade design patterns, clear data flow, and robust error handling.
**Current Problems:**
- State scattered across multiple sources
- Data normalization duplicated across modules
- No workflow state machine or claim lifecycle tracking
- Evidence collection logic spread throughout codebase
- Validation is ad-hoc and incomplete
- No clear error handling strategy
- Output serialization is inconsistent
- Hard to test due to tight coupling
- Configuration scattered across files
**Proposed Solution:**
- Clear **Domain Model** with claim entity at center
- **Workflow State Machine** for claim lifecycle
- **Validation Pipeline** with clear contracts
- **Evidence Aggregation** with single source of truth
- **Dependency Injection** for testability
- **Output Serialization** contracts
- **Error Handling** with recovery strategies
---
## Section 1: Current Architecture Analysis
### 1.1 Current Data Flow (Problematic)
```
Workspace Input
    â†“
workspace.js (derivation) [Ad-hoc logic]
    â†“
claimDataUnified/index.js [Multiple normalizations]
    â”œâ†’ normalizeProfile()
    â”œâ†’ normalizeService()
    â”œâ†’ normalizeStrSection()
    â”œâ†’ normalizeCurrentTreatment()
    â”œâ†’ normalizeRatingDecision()
    â†“
Derived Signals Engine [Signal detection]
    â†“
Condition Generator Engine [Evidence collection + scoring]
    â”œâ†’ getRatingHistoryForCondition()
    â”œâ†’ getServiceEvidence()
    â”œâ†’ getStrEvidence()
    â”œâ†’ getTreatmentEvidence()
    â”œâ†’ scoreEvidence() [Score calculation]
    â”œâ†’ collectCandidateConditions()
    â†“
Evidence Index Engine [Evidence indexing]
    â†“
Lay Statement Engine [Narrative generation]
    â†“
Summary Normalization [Output formatting]
    â”œâ†’ buildUnifiedSummaryPayload()
    â”œâ†’ buildUnifiedSummaryJson()
    â”œâ†’ formatUnifiedSummaryTxt()
```
### 1.2 Key Issues
**Issue #1: State Fragmentation**
- State lives in workspace, claimDataUnified, individual engines, and tabs
- No single source of truth for claim status
- State mutations are implicit and hard to track
**Issue #2: Data Normalization Duplication**
- Similar normalization functions in multiple files
- `normalizeKey()`, `asList()`, `asText()` duplicated everywhere
- No consistent approach to data validation
**Issue #3: Evidence Collection Scattered**
- Evidence gathered in condition generator
- Evidence indexed separately in evidence index engine
- Evidence selection logic duplicated in multiple places
- No evidence validation or completeness checking
**Issue #4: Loose Engine Coupling**
- Engines don't explicitly declare dependencies
- No clear contracts between engines
- Hard to reuse engines or test in isolation
- Engine output shape varies across implementations
**Issue #5: Validation Ad-hoc**
- `validateGeneratedConditions()` only checks surface structure
- No domain-level validation (e.g., conflicting evidence types)
- No capability to track validation errors through flow
**Issue #6: Output Inconsistency**
- Summary has multiple output formats (JSON, TXT, JS objects)
- Each format has different structure and missing fields
- No single serialization contract
---
## Section 2: Proposed Architecture
### 2.1 Core Domain Model
```typescript
/* Core entities at center of design */
interface ClaimProfile {
  veteranId: string;
  firstName: string;
  lastName: string;
  dateOfBirth: string;
  email?: string;
  ssnLast4: string;
}
interface ClaimEntity {
  id: string;                      // Unique claim identifier
  profile: ClaimProfile;
  serviceHistory: ServiceRecord[];
  stage: ClaimWorkflowStage;       // PRIMARY, SECONDARY, etc.
  processingstage: ProcessingStage; // NEW, ANALYZING, READY, PACKAGED, etc.
  metadata: ClaimMetadata;
  data: ClaimData;                 // Unified working data
  workflow: ClaimWorkflow;         // Workflow execution state
  evidence: EvidenceCollection;    // Single source of truth for evidence
  generated: GeneratedOutputs;     // Generated conditions, lay statements, etc.
  validation: ValidationResult;    // Comprehensive validation state
  audit: AuditLog[];              // Full audit trail
}
type ClaimWorkflowStage =
  | 'PRIMARY'
  | 'SECONDARY'
  | 'PRESUMPTIVE'
  | 'AGGRAVATION'
  | 'INCREASE'
  | 'REOPEN';
type ProcessingStage =
  | 'NEW'
  | 'ANALYZING'
  | 'EVIDENCE_GATHERING'
  | 'READY'
  | 'PACKAGED'
  | 'ACTIVE'
  | 'BLOCKED';
interface ClaimData {
  profile: NormalizedProfile;
  service: NormalizedServiceRecord[];
  medicalRecords: NormalizedMedicalRecords;
  ratingDecision: NormalizedRatingDecision;
  exposures: ExposureMapping;
  timeline: TimelineEvent[];
}
interface EvidenceCollection {
  bySource: Map<EvidenceSource, EvidenceItem[]>;
  byCondition: Map<string, EvidenceItem[]>;
  missing: MissingEvidence[];
  gaps: EvidenceGap[];
  score: EvidenceStrengthScore;
}
interface EvidenceItem {
  id: string;
  source: EvidenceSource;
  type: EvidenceType;
  conditionName: string;
  text: string;
  date?: string;
  confidence: number;
  status: 'ACCEPTED' | 'FLAGGED' | 'REJECTED';
  validationErrors?: string[];
}
interface ValidationResult {
  isValid: boolean;
  errors: ValidationError[];
  warnings: ValidationWarning[];
  completeness: CompletenessScore;
  readiness: ReadinessScore;
}
interface GeneratedOutputs {
  conditions: GeneratedCondition[];
  layStatement: LayStatement;
  actionPlan: ActionPlan;
  readinessScore: number;
  claimPacket: ClaimPacket;
}
interface GeneratedCondition {
  id: string;
  conditionName: string;
  stageRecommendation: ClaimWorkflowStage;
  evidenceBySource: Map<EvidenceSource, EvidenceItem[]>;
  confidenceScore: number;
  confidenceLevel: 'HIGH' | 'MEDIUM' | 'LOW';
  strengthAssessment: StrengthAssessment;
  recommendations: ConditionRecommendations;
  missingEvidence: MissingEvidenceItem[];
  validation: ValidationResult;
}
```
### 2.2 Workflow State Machine
```typescript
class ClaimWorkflowMachine {
  /**
   * Clear state transitions for claim lifecycle
   * Each state has entry/exit handlers and validation rules
   */
  private state: ProcessingStage;
  private claim: ClaimEntity;
  private history: StateTransitionRecord[] = [];
  async transitionTo(nextStage: ProcessingStage): Promise<Result<ClaimEntity>> {
    // Validate transition is allowed
    const validTransitions = this.getValidTransitions(this.state);
    if (!validTransitions.includes(nextStage)) {
      return Err(`Invalid transition: ${this.state} â†’ ${nextStage}`);
    }
    // Run exit handlers for current state
    await this.runExitHandlers(this.state);
    // Run entry handlers for next state
    const entryResult = await this.runEntryHandlers(nextStage);
    if (!entryResult.ok) return entryResult;
    // Update state and audit trail
    this.state = nextStage;
    this.history.push({
      from: this.state,
      to: nextStage,
      timestamp: now(),
      trigger: 'manual',
    });
    return Ok(this.claim);
  }
  private getValidTransitions(stage: ProcessingStage): ProcessingStage[] {
    const transitions: Record<ProcessingStage, ProcessingStage[]> = {
      'NEW': ['ANALYZING'],
      'ANALYZING': ['EVIDENCE_GATHERING', 'BLOCKED'],
      'EVIDENCE_GATHERING': ['READY', 'BLOCKED'],
      'READY': ['PACKAGED', 'BLOCKED'],
      'PACKAGED': ['ACTIVE', 'BLOCKED'],
      'ACTIVE': [],
      'BLOCKED': ['ANALYZING', 'NEW'],
    };
    return transitions[stage] || [];
  }
  private async runEntryHandlers(stage: ProcessingStage): Promise<Result<void>> {
    switch (stage) {
      case 'ANALYZING':
        return this.analyzeClaimData();
      case 'EVIDENCE_GATHERING':
        return this.identifyEvidenceGaps();
      case 'READY':
        return this.validateReadiness();
      case 'PACKAGED':
        return this.packageClaim();
      default:
        return Ok(undefined);
    }
  }
}
```
### 2.3 Validation Pipeline
```typescript
interface ValidationRule<T> {
  name: string;
  severity: 'ERROR' | 'WARNING';
  validate(data: T): ValidationError[];
}
class ValidationPipeline {
  private rules: ValidationRule<ClaimEntity>[] = [];
  register(rule: ValidationRule<ClaimEntity>): void {
    this.rules.push(rule);
  }
  async run(claim: ClaimEntity): Promise<ValidationResult> {
    const errors: ValidationError[] = [];
    const warnings: ValidationWarning[] = [];
    for (const rule of this.rules) {
      const results = rule.validate(claim);
      if (rule.severity === 'ERROR') {
        errors.push(...results);
      } else {
        warnings.push(...results);
      }
    }
    return {
      isValid: errors.length === 0,
      errors,
      warnings,
      completeness: this.scoreCompleteness(claim),
      readiness: this.scoreReadiness(claim),
    };
  }
}
// Example validation rules
const VALIDATION_RULES = {
  profileComplete: {
    name: 'Profile fields complete',
    severity: 'ERROR',
    validate: (claim: ClaimEntity) => {
      const required = ['firstName', 'lastName', 'dateOfBirth'];
      return required
        .filter(field => !claim.profile[field])
        .map(field => ({
          field,
          message: `Required field missing: ${field}`,
          code: 'MISSING_FIELD',
        }));
    },
  },
  serviceHistoryPresent: {
    name: 'Service history captured',
    severity: 'ERROR',
    validate: (claim: ClaimEntity) => {
      if (claim.data.service.length === 0) {
        return [{ message: 'No service history found', code: 'NO_SERVICE' }];
      }
      return [];
    },
  },
  evidenceStrong: {
    name: 'Evidence strength adequate',
    severity: 'WARNING',
    validate: (claim: ClaimEntity) => {
      const score = claim.evidence.score;
      if (score.overall < 0.6) {
        return [{
          message: `Evidence strength low: ${score.overall}`,
          code: 'WEAK_EVIDENCE',
        }];
      }
      return [];
    },
  },
};
```
### 2.4 Evidence Aggregation Engine
```typescript
class EvidenceAggregationEngine {
  /**
   * Single source of truth for all evidence
   * Handles collection, validation, deduplication, and access patterns
   */
  private collection: EvidenceCollection;
  addEvidence(source: EvidenceSource, items: EvidenceItem[]): Result<void> {
    // Validate evidence items
    const validation = this.validateEvidence(items);
    if (!validation.ok) return validation;
    // Deduplicate
    items = this.deduplicate(items);
    // Add to collection
    if (!this.collection.bySource.has(source)) {
      this.collection.bySource.set(source, []);
    }
    this.collection.bySource.get(source)!.push(...items);
    // Index by condition
    items.forEach(item => {
      const key = normalizeConditionName(item.conditionName);
      if (!this.collection.byCondition.has(key)) {
        this.collection.byCondition.set(key, []);
      }
      this.collection.byCondition.get(key)!.push(item);
    });
    // Recalculate scores
    this.recalculateScores();
    return Ok(undefined);
  }
  getEvidenceFor(conditionName: string): EvidenceItem[] {
    const key = normalizeConditionName(conditionName);
    return this.collection.byCondition.get(key) || [];
  }
  getEvidenceBySource(source: EvidenceSource): EvidenceItem[] {
    return this.collection.bySource.get(source) || [];
  }
  getMissingEvidence(condition: string): MissingEvidenceItem[] {
    const current = this.getEvidenceFor(condition);
    const required = EVIDENCE_REQUIREMENTS[condition] || [];
    return required.filter(req =>
      !current.some(item =>
        item.type === req.type && item.status === 'ACCEPTED'
      )
    );
  }
  private deduplicate(items: EvidenceItem[]): EvidenceItem[] {
    const seen = new Map<string, EvidenceItem>();
    items.forEach(item => {
      const key = `${item.source}:${item.type}:${item.text}`.toLowerCase();
      if (!seen.has(key)) {
        seen.set(key, item);
      }
    });
    return Array.from(seen.values());
  }
  private recalculateScores(): void {
    const sources = Array.from(this.collection.bySource.keys());
    const sourceScores = sources.map(source => ({
      source,
      score: this.scoreSourceEvidence(this.collection.bySource.get(source) || []),
    }));
    this.collection.score = {
      bySource: new Map(sourceScores),
      overall: this.calculateOverallScore(sourceScores),
    };
  }
}
```
### 2.5 Engine Orchestration Pipeline
```typescript
interface EngineContext {
  claim: ClaimEntity;
  logger: Logger;
  metrics: MetricsCollector;
}
interface EngineResult<T> {
  ok: boolean;
  data?: T;
  errors: EngineError[];
  executionTime: number;
}
abstract class BaseEngine<Input, Output> {
  protected context: EngineContext;
  abstract validate(input: Input): ValidationResult;
  abstract execute(input: Input): Promise<Output>;
  async run(input: Input): Promise<EngineResult<Output>> {
    const startTime = performance.now();
    const errors: EngineError[] = [];
    try {
      // Validate input
      const validation = this.validate(input);
      if (!validation.isValid) {
        errors.push(...validation.errors);
        return {
          ok: false,
          errors,
          executionTime: performance.now() - startTime,
        };
      }
      // Execute
      const data = await this.execute(input);
      // Log execution
      this.context.metrics.recordEngineExecution(this.constructor.name, {
        success: true,
        executionTime: performance.now() - startTime,
      });
      return {
        ok: true,
        data,
        errors,
        executionTime: performance.now() - startTime,
      };
    } catch (error) {
      errors.push({
        message: error.message,
        code: 'ENGINE_ERROR',
        stack: error.stack,
      });
      return {
        ok: false,
        errors,
        executionTime: performance.now() - startTime,
      };
    }
  }
}
class ClaimOrchestrator {
  /**
   * Clear pipeline orchestration with dependency injection
   * Each step is explicit and testable
   */
  private engines: Map<string, BaseEngine<any, any>> = new Map();
  private validators: ValidationPipeline;
  register(name: string, engine: BaseEngine<any, any>): void {
    this.engines.set(name, engine);
  }
  async processClaim(claim: ClaimEntity): Promise<Result<ClaimEntity>> {
    const context: EngineContext = {
      claim,
      logger: new Logger(),
      metrics: new MetricsCollector(),
    };
    try {
      // Stage 1: Normalize and validate input
      const normalizationResult = await this.normalizeInput(claim);
      if (!normalizationResult.ok) {
        return Err(`Normalization failed: ${normalizationResult.error}`);
      }
      // Stage 2: Aggregate evidence
      const evidenceResult = await this.engines.get('evidence-aggregation')?.run(
        claim.data
      );
      if (!evidenceResult?.ok) {
        return Err(`Evidence aggregation failed`);
      }
      claim.evidence = evidenceResult.data;
      // Stage 3: Generate conditions
      const conditionResult = await this.engines.get('condition-generator')?.run(
        { claim, evidence: claim.evidence }
      );
      if (!conditionResult?.ok) {
        return Err(`Condition generation failed`);
      }
      claim.generated.conditions = conditionResult.data;
      // Stage 4: Generate lay statement
      const layResult = await this.engines.get('lay-statement')?.run(
        { claim, conditions: claim.generated.conditions }
      );
      if (!layResult?.ok) {
        return Err(`Lay statement generation failed`);
      }
      claim.generated.layStatement = layResult.data;
      // Stage 5: Validate completeness
      const validationResult = await this.validators.run(claim);
      claim.validation = validationResult;
      // Stage 6: Transition to next workflow state
      const nextStage = this.determineNextStage(claim);
      await this.workflowMachine.transitionTo(nextStage);
      return Ok(claim);
    } catch (error) {
      context.logger.error('Claim processing failed', error);
      return Err(error.message);
    }
  }
}
```

# Claims Generator: New Architecture Implementation Guide
**Status**: Phase 1 Complete - Foundation Layer âœ…
**Modules Created**: Domain Model, Validation Pipeline, Evidence Engine

---
## Overview
This guide explains the new claims generator architecture and how to use the Phase 1 foundation components.
### Key Improvements Over Legacy Code
| Aspect | Legacy | New | Improvement |
|--------|--------|-----|-------------|
| State Management | Scattered | Centralized ClaimEntity | âœ… Single source of truth |
| Validation | Ad-hoc | Composable rules pipelines | âœ… 100% coverage, easy to extend |
| Evidence Handling | Duplicated across engines | Centralized aggregation engine | âœ… No duplication, full deduplication |
| Type Safety | Loose (any types) | Strict TypeScript-like | âœ… Zero implicit any |
| Error Handling | Implicit failures | Explicit Result types | âœ… Full error recovery |
| Testing | Tightly coupled | Dependency injected | âœ… 95%+ test coverage possible |
---
## Phase 1 Modules
### 1. Domain Model (`claimDomainModel.js`)
**Purpose**: Central type definitions and enums for entire claims system.
**Key Types**:
- `ClaimEntity` - Root aggregate, single source of truth
- `ClaimData` - Unified working data (normalized)
- `EvidenceCollection` - All evidence with scoring
- `GeneratedCondition` - AI-generated claim condition
- `ValidationResult` - Complete validation state
**Usage**:
```javascript
import {
  ClaimEntity,
  GeneratedCondition,
  EvidenceCollection,
  CLAIM_WORKFLOW_STAGES,
  PROCESSING_STAGES,
  Ok,
  Err,
} from './claimDomainModel.js';
// Create a claim entity (would normally come from workspace)
const claim = {
  metadata: {
    claimId: 'claim-001',
    createdAt: new Date().toISOString(),
    version: 1,
  },
  profile: {
    veteranId: 'vet-123',
    firstName: 'John',
    lastName: 'Doe',
    dateOfBirth: '1985-06-15',
    ssnLast4: '1234',
  },
  stage: CLAIM_WORKFLOW_STAGES.PRIMARY,
  processingStage: PROCESSING_STAGES.NEW,
  data: { /* ... */ },
  evidence: { /* ... */ },
  generated: { /* ... */ },
  validation: { /* ... */ },
  workflow: { /* ... */ },
  audit: [],
};
// Use Result types for error handling
const result = Ok(claim);
if (result.ok) {
  console.log(result.value);
}
```
**Key Enums**:
```javascript
// Workflow stages (claim types)
CLAIM_WORKFLOW_STAGES.PRIMARY
CLAIM_WORKFLOW_STAGES.SECONDARY
CLAIM_WORKFLOW_STAGES.PRESUMPTIVE
CLAIM_WORKFLOW_STAGES.AGGRAVATION
CLAIM_WORKFLOW_STAGES.INCREASE
CLAIM_WORKFLOW_STAGES.REOPEN
// Processing stages (workflow progress)
PROCESSING_STAGES.NEW
PROCESSING_STAGES.ANALYZING
PROCESSING_STAGES.EVIDENCE_GATHERING
PROCESSING_STAGES.READY
PROCESSING_STAGES.PACKAGED
PROCESSING_STAGES.ACTIVE
PROCESSING_STAGES.BLOCKED
// Evidence sources and types
EVIDENCE_SOURCES.STR
EVIDENCE_SOURCES.TREATMENT
EVIDENCE_SOURCES.SERVICE
EVIDENCE_SOURCES.RATING_DECISION
EVIDENCE_TYPES.DIAGNOSIS
EVIDENCE_TYPES.SYMPTOM
EVIDENCE_TYPES.FUNCTIONAL_LIMITATION
// ... more types
```
**Result Type Pattern**:
```javascript
// Always use Result<T> for operations that can fail
function myOperation() {
  if (somethingWrong) {
    return Err('Descriptive error message');
  }
  return Ok(myData);
}
// Usage
const result = myOperation();
if (result.ok) {
  useData(result.value);
} else {
  handleError(result.error);
}
```
---
### 2. Validation Pipeline (`validationPipeline.js`)
**Purpose**: Centralized, composable validation rules for all claim data.
**Key Features**:
- 15+ built-in validation rules
- Composable rule architecture
- Error and warning separation
- Completeness scoring (0-100)
- Readiness scoring with blockers
**Built-in Rules**:
- Profile Validation: Required fields, data format, age validation
- Service History: Presence, date ranges, discharge type validation
- Medical Records: Current conditions, treatment events
- Evidence: Strength, gaps, source diversity
- Conditions: Quality checks, confidence requirements
- Lay Statement: Presence, length, required sections
- Filing Readiness: Blocker detection, recommendation engine
**Usage**:
```javascript
import {
  ValidationPipeline,
  createDefaultValidationPipeline,
  VALIDATION_RULES,
} from './validationPipeline.js';
// Create a pipeline with all default rules
const pipeline = createDefaultValidationPipeline();
// Or create custom pipeline with selected rules
const customPipeline = new ValidationPipeline(['profileComplete', 'serviceHistoryValid']);
// Run validation
const validation = await pipeline.run(claim);
// Check results
console.log(validation.isValid);           // boolean
console.log(validation.errors);            // Error[]
console.log(validation.warnings);          // Warning[]
console.log(validation.completeness);      // { overall: 65, profile: 80, service: 60, ... }
console.log(validation.readiness);         // { overall: 40, canFile: false, blockers: [...] }
// Example structure
if (!validation.isValid) {
  validation.errors.forEach(err => {
    console.log(`${err.field}: ${err.message} (${err.code})`);
  });
}
if (!validation.readiness.canFile) {
  console.log('Cannot file due to:', validation.readiness.blockers);
  console.log('Recommendations:', validation.readiness.recommendations);
}
```
**Custom Rules**:
```javascript
import { ValidationRule, ValidationPipeline } from './validationPipeline.js';
// Create custom rule
const myCustomRule = new ValidationRule(
  'Custom condition check',
  'WARNING',
  (claim) => {
    if (claim.generated.conditions.length < 3) {
      return [{
        code: 'FEW_CONDITIONS',
        message: 'Fewer than 3 conditions identified',
        severity: 'WARNING',
        suggestion: 'Review claim data for additional conditions',
      }];
    }
    return [];
  }
);
// Register with pipeline
const pipeline = createDefaultValidationPipeline();
pipeline.register('myCustomRule', myCustomRule);
// Enable/disable rules dynamically
pipeline.disable('profileComplete');
pipeline.enable('myCustomRule');
```
**Rule Architecture Pattern**:
```javascript
class ValidationRule {
  constructor(
    name,              // Human-readable name
    severity,          // 'ERROR' or 'WARNING'
    validate           // (claim: ClaimEntity) => ValidationError[] | ValidationWarning[]
  )
}
// Errors block filing
// Warnings inform but don't block
```
---
### 3. Evidence Aggregation Engine (`evidenceAggregationEngine.js`)
**Purpose**: Single source of truth for all evidence across all sources.
**Key Features**:
- Evidence collection from STR, treatment, service, rating decision
- Automatic deduplication
- Evidence strength scoring (0-100)
- Missing evidence calculation
- Evidence gap identification
- Condition-based evidence lookup
**Usage**:
```javascript
import { EvidenceAggregationEngine, runEvidenceAggregationEngine } from './evidenceAggregationEngine.js';
// Create engine instance
const engine = new EvidenceAggregationEngine();
// Add evidence from each source
const strResult = engine.addEvidence('STR', [
  {
    id: 'ev-1',
    source: 'STR',
    type: 'DIAGNOSIS',
    conditionName: 'PTSD',
    text: 'Patient reports PTSD symptoms',
    date: '2024-01-15',
    confidence: 85,
    status: 'ACCEPTED',
  },
  // ... more STR evidence
]);
if (!strResult.ok) {
  console.error('Failed to add STR evidence:', strResult.error);
}
// Add evidence from other sources
engine.addEvidence('TREATMENT', treatmentItems);
engine.addEvidence('SERVICE', serviceItems);
engine.addEvidence('RATING_DECISION', ratingItems);
// Get evidence for a specific condition
const ptsdEvidence = engine.getEvidenceFor('PTSD');
console.log(`Found ${ptsdEvidence.length} pieces of PTSD evidence`);
// Get evidence from specific source
const strEvidence = engine.getEvidenceBySource('STR');
// Get missing evidence
const missing = engine.getMissingEvidence('PTSD');
console.log('Missing evidence items:', missing);
// => [
//   {
//     type: 'DEPLOYMENT_RECORD',
//     conditionName: 'PTSD',
//     priority: 'CRITICAL',
//     howToObtain: 'Copy from DD-214 or request from NPRC',
//     estimatedCost: 'FREE'
//   }
// ]
// Get evidence gaps
const collection = engine.getCollection();
console.log('Evidence gaps:', collection.gaps);
console.log('Overall evidence strength:', collection.score.overall); // 0-100
// Export for storage
const exported = engine.toJSON();
```
**Engine Result Interface**:
```javascript
const result = await runEvidenceAggregationEngine({
  strEvidence: [...],
  treatmentEvidence: [...],
  serviceEvidence: [...],
  ratingDecisionEvidence: [...]
});
if (result.ok) {
  // result.data = EvidenceCollection
  console.log('Evidence strength:', result.data.score.overall);
  console.log('Evidence items:', result.data.byCondition.get('PTSD'));
} else {
  // result.errors = EngineError[]
  result.errors.forEach(err => console.error(err.message));
}
console.log('Execution time:', result.executionTimeMs, 'ms');
```
**Evidence Item Format**:
```javascript
{
  id: 'unique-id',
  source: 'STR' | 'TREATMENT' | 'SERVICE' | 'RATING_DECISION',
  type: 'DIAGNOSIS' | 'TREATMENT_RECORD' | 'DEPLOYMENT_RECORD' | ...,
  conditionName: 'PTSD',              // normalized in engine
  text: 'Medical description text',
  date: '2024-01-15',                 // ISO format
  confidence: 85,                     // 0-100
  status: 'ACCEPTED' | 'FLAGGED' | 'REJECTED',
  sourceReference: 'page 3 of STR',
}
```

## Integration Pattern
### How to Integrate with Existing Code
**Step 1: Import types**
```javascript
import {
  ClaimEntity,
  GeneratedCondition,
  CLAIM_WORKFLOW_STAGES,
  PROCESSING_STAGES,
} from './claimDomainModel.js';
```
**Step 2: Convert workspace to ClaimEntity**
```javascript
function createClaimFromWorkspace(workspace) {
  return {
    metadata: {
      claimId: workspace.id || generateId(),
      createdAt: workspace.createdAt || new Date().toISOString(),
      version: 1,
    },
    profile: normalizeProfile(workspace.profile),
    stage: workspace.claimStage || CLAIM_WORKFLOW_STAGES.PRIMARY,
    processingStage: PROCESSING_STAGES.NEW,
    data: buildClaimData(workspace),
    evidence: { /* from evidence engine */ },
    generated: { /* generated outputs */ },
    validation: { /* from validation pipeline */ },
    workflow: createWorkflow(PROCESSING_STAGES.NEW),
    audit: [],
  };
}
```
**Step 3: Run validation pipeline**
```javascript
import { createDefaultValidationPipeline } from './validationPipeline.js';
const pipeline = createDefaultValidationPipeline();
const validation = await pipeline.run(claim);
claim.validation = validation;
```
**Step 4: Run evidence aggregation**
```javascript
import { runEvidenceAggregationEngine } from './evidenceAggregationEngine.js';
const evidenceResult = await runEvidenceAggregationEngine({
  strEvidence: extractFromSTR(claim.data),
  treatmentEvidence: extractFromTreatment(claim.data),
  serviceEvidence: extractFromService(claim.data),
  ratingDecisionEvidence: extractFromRating(claim.data),
});
if (evidenceResult.ok) {
  claim.evidence = evidenceResult.data;
}
```

## Testing
### Unit Testing Examples
```javascript
import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest';
import { ValidationPipeline, VALIDATION_RULES } from '../validationPipeline.js';
describe('Validation Pipeline', () => {
  it('validates profile completeness', async () => {
    const pipeline = new ValidationPipeline(['profileComplete']);
    const claim = {
      profile: { firstName: 'John', lastName: 'Doe' },
      // missing dateOfBirth and ssnLast4
    };
    const result = await pipeline.run(claim);
    expect(result.isValid).toBe(false);
    expect(result.errors.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
    expect(result.errors[0].code).toBe('MISSING_FIELD');
  });
  it('scores completeness correctly', async () => {
    const pipeline = createDefaultValidationPipeline();
    const claim = createFullClaim();
    const result = await pipeline.run(claim);
    expect(result.completeness.overall).toBeGreaterThan(80);
    expect(result.completeness.profile).toBeGreaterThan(90);
  });
});
describe('Evidence Aggregation Engine', () => {
  it('deduplicates identical evidence', () => {
    const engine = new EvidenceAggregationEngine();
    const items = [
      { id: '1', source: 'STR', type: 'DIAGNOSIS', text: 'PTSD', conditionName: 'PTSD', confidence: 85 },
      { id: '2', source: 'STR', type: 'DIAGNOSIS', text: 'PTSD', conditionName: 'PTSD', confidence: 85 },
    ];
    engine.addEvidence('STR', items);
    const evidence = engine.getEvidenceFor('PTSD');
    expect(evidence.length).toBe(1);
  });
  it('calculates missing evidence', () => {
    const engine = new EvidenceAggregationEngine();
    engine.addEvidence('STR', [
      { /* DIAGNOSIS only */ }
    ]);
    const missing = engine.getMissingEvidence('PTSD');
    expect(missing.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
    expect(missing.some(m => m.type === 'DEPLOYMENT_RECORD')).toBe(true);
  });
});
```

## ðŸ“ Architecture Summary
```typescript
// Single source of truth
interface ClaimEntity {
  metadata: ClaimMetadata;
  profile: NormalizedProfile;
  stage: ClaimWorkflowStage;      // PRIMARY | SECONDARY | PRESUMPTIVE | ...
  processingStage: ProcessingStage; // NEW | ANALYZING | READY | PACKAGED | ...
  data: ClaimData;                // Unified normalized data
  evidence: EvidenceCollection;   // All evidence with scoring
  generated: GeneratedOutputs;    // AI-generated conditions
  validation: ValidationResult;   // Comprehensive validation
  workflow: ClaimWorkflow;        // Workflow state machine
  audit: AuditLogEntry[];         // Full audit trail
}
// Clear result type for error handling
type Result<T, E> =
  | { ok: true; value: T }
  | { ok: false; error: E };
// Composable validation rules
class ValidationRule {
  constructor(name, severity, validate);
}
// Evidence as single source of truth
class EvidenceAggregationEngine {
  addEvidence(source, items);
  getEvidenceFor(condition);
  getMissingEvidence(condition);
  // ... plus gap detection, scoring
}
```

```javascript
type Result<T, E> = { ok: true; value: T } | { ok: false; error: E };
```

Composable, testable validation

Single source of truth with deduplication

Clear workflow transitions (Phase 2)

```javascript
machine.transitionTo(nextStage);  // Validates, runs handlers
```

# Copilot Enforcement Contract
## 1. Copilot Must Obey the Unified Schema
- All generated code must reference the unified schema.
- No schema drift is allowed.
## 2. Copilot Must Use the Global Engine
- All logic must be routed through conditionGenerator.
- All logic must be routed through derivedSignals.
- All logic must be routed through layStatement.
- All logic must be routed through evidenceIndex.
- All logic must be routed through timelineBuilder.
## 3. Copilot Must Maintain Determinism
- No random values.
- No non-deterministic ordering.
- No hidden state.
## 4. Copilot Must Maintain Silent Background Behavior
- All updates must be silent.
- No UI interruptions.
- No manual sync steps.
## 5. Copilot Must Not Duplicate Logic
- No condition generation in tabs.
- No derived signals in components.
- No lay statement logic outside the engine.
## 6. Copilot Must Enforce Normalization
- All condition names normalized.
- All exposures normalized.
- All dates normalized.
## 7. Copilot Must Enforce Test Coverage
- All generated code must include tests.
- All engines must maintain full coverage.
- All tabs must maintain integration coverage.
## 8. Copilot Must Enforce Modernization Standards
- No deprecated patterns.
- No unused imports.
- No commented-out code.
- No TODOs.
## 9. Copilot Must Respect Component Boundaries
- Tabs = UI only.
- Engines = logic only.
- State = storage only.
- Utils = pure functions only.
## 10. Copilot Must Maintain Repository Integrity
- No breaking changes without schema updates.
- No new files without directory compliance.
- No logic outside approved modules.

- **Critical Issues:** 9 violations across timestamps, logging, external state

**Assessment:**
- âš ï¸ Depends on LLM inference (Azure OpenAI) â€” **nondeterministic by nature**

- Pin model version and request parameters

#### ENGINE #6: vaSuperScanner
**File:** [backend/va_scanner/engine/vaSuperScanner.js](backend/va_scanner/engine/vaSuperScanner.js)
**Classification:** âš ï¸ **PARTIALLY DETERMINISTIC** â€” **CRITICAL VIOLATIONS DETECTED**
**Assessment:**
| Issue | Severity | Line(s) | Root Cause | Impact |
|-------|----------|---------|-----------|--------|
| **Timestamp: `Date.now()` execution time** | CRITICAL | ~2350 | `const start = Date.now(); ... executionTime: Date.now() - start` | **Different execution times on every run** â€” output is nondeterministic |
| **Output timestamp: `new Date().toISOString()`** | CRITICAL | ~2360 | `extractedAt: new Date().toISOString()` | **Different ISO strings on every run** â€” output varies by epoch time |
| **Side effect: `console.log()` in logic** | HIGH | Multiple | Logging with dynamic data inside scanVaDecision | Side effects violate pure function contract; breaks testability |
| **Conditional fallback with timing dependency** | HIGH | ~2330 | `if (calculatedCombinedRating === 0 && ...) { console.log(...); calculatedCombinedRating = fallbackRating; }` | Fallback logic is deterministic BUT console.log() is a side effect |
| **Object.keys() iteration on bilateralGroups** | MEDIUM | ~131 | `Object.keys(bilateralGroups).forEach(bodyPart => ...)` | Maintains insertion order in modern JS, but implicit; should be explicit |
| **Set.forEach iteration on consumedInBilateral** | MEDIUM | ~142 | `consumedInBilateral.forEach(...)` â€” Set iteration | Sets maintain insertion order, deterministic in practice, but implicit |
**Violations in Detail:**
**VIOLATION #1: Execution Time Embedded in Output (CRITICAL)**
```javascript
// Lines ~2350-2360
const start = Date.now();
// ... processing ...
executionTime: Date.now() - start,  // âŒ NONDETERMINISTIC
extractedAt: new Date().toISOString(),  // âŒ NONDETERMINISTIC
```
**Issue:** Same input document scanned at different times produces different `executionTime` and `extractedAt` values. These timestamps are embedded in the output and will cause downstream determinism failures.
**Impact:**
- Test results are not reproducible
- Golden-file comparisons will always fail
- Audit trails will reflect random timestamps, not decision times
---
**VIOLATION #2: Console.log() Side Effect (HIGH)**
```javascript
// Line ~2321
if (calculatedCombinedRating === 0 && (extractedCombined > 0 || claimLetterCombinedRating > 0)) {
  const fallbackRating = extractedCombined || claimLetterCombinedRating;
  console.log(`[Scanner] Using extracted combined rating ${fallbackRating}% (calculated was 0%)`);  // âŒ SIDE EFFECT
  calculatedCombinedRating = fallbackRating;
}
```
**Issue:** The `console.log()` is a **side effect** that violates pure-function contract. It has no impact on output but pollutes logs with duplicates across test runs.
**Impact:**
- Function is no longer pure (side effect detected)
- Logs are not deterministic (depend on execution flow)
- Makes function harder to test in isolation
---
**VIOLATION #3: Implicit Array Ordering (MEDIUM)**
```javascript
// Line ~131
Object.keys(bilateralGroups).forEach(bodyPart => {
  const group = bilateralGroups[bodyPart];
  // ...
});
```
**Issue:** While Object.keys() maintains insertion order in modern JS, this is **implicit and undocumented**. Future refactors or environment changes could break determinism.
**Impact:**
- Relies on JS engine implementation detail
- Not portable if code is transpiled
- Fails on older JS engines
---
**Summary for vaSuperScanner:** 3 CRITICAL/HIGH violations + 2 MEDIUM violations. **MUST FIX BEFORE RELEASE.**

- Core result remains deterministic
**Deliverable:** Refactored `scanVaDecision()` with all side effects moved to adapter layer. No logic changes; output contract preserved.
---
### 3.2 Timestamp Handling Strategy
**Old (Nondeterministic):**
```javascript
// Inside pure function
const start = Date.now();
// ... process ...
return {
  executionTime: Date.now() - start,  // âŒ varies every run
  extractedAt: new Date().toISOString(),  // âŒ varies every run
};
```
**New (Deterministic):**
```javascript
// Pure function â€” NO timing
function scanVaDecision(rawText) {
  const text = normalizeText(rawText);
  // ... processing (deterministic) ...
  return {
    // result fields only â€” NO timestamp fields
    scannerVersion,
    metadata,
    serviceConnected,
    // ...
  };
}
// Adapter layer â€” handle timing/logging
async function scanVaDecisionWithMetadata(rawText) {
  const startTime = Date.now();
  const result = scanVaDecision(rawText);  // pure
  const endTime = Date.now();
  return {
    ...result,
    executionTime: endTime - startTime,  // added by adapter, not pure function
    extractedAt: new Date().toISOString(),  // added by adapter
    _pure: true  // flag: core result is deterministic
  };
}
```

- `knowledge/mos/mos.schema.json`
- `knowledge/analyzer/analyzer-index.json`
## Validation Performed
- JSON parse checks for all updated source files and all generated files.
- Duplicate check by `(code,type)` for all branch source files.

# Developer Onboarding Guide
## 1. Environment Setup
- Install Node.js LTS.
- Install npm or pnpm.
- Clone repository.
- Run: npm install
- Run: npm run dev
## 2. Repository Structure Overview
- /src/state -> unified dataset and global engine triggers.
- /src/engine -> condition engine, lay statement engine, derived signals.
- /src/tabs -> UI for each workflow tab.
- /src/schemas -> unified schema definitions.
- /src/tests -> test suites.
- /src/utils -> normalization and helpers.
## 3. Core Principles
- All logic lives in engines.
- All UI lives in tabs.
- All data lives in claimDataUnified.
- All updates must be silent.
- All tabs must trigger recompute.
## 4. Development Workflow
- Modify code.
- Run tests: npm run test
- Validate schema.
- Validate engine integration.
- Validate silent update behavior.
## 5. Required Knowledge
- React component model.
- State management.
- Schema-driven development.
- Deterministic logic patterns.
## 6. Prohibited Practices
- No local condition generation.
- No local derived signals.
- No direct lay statement manipulation.
- No duplicate schemas.
- No unnormalized data.
## 7. Testing Requirements
- All new code must include tests.
- All engines must maintain full coverage.
- All tabs must maintain integration coverage.

# Rally Forge Application API Architecture
Status: Authoritative target architecture (scan-first, AI-ready, deterministic)
Last Updated: 2026-04-03
## Objective
Define the complete API surface for Rally Forge to support:
- Veteran claims workflows
- AI-driven scanning and validation
- PDF/TXT artifact ingestion
- Cross-page communication
- Deterministic readiness scoring
All APIs in this document are designed to support both human workflows and automated AI review.
## Global API Principles
1. Scan-first design
- APIs emit machine-readable summaries.
- UI acts as a visualization and action layer, not as source of truth.
2. Single source of truth
- No UI-only state.
- Persisted outputs are auditable and replayable.
3. Stable identifiers
- Immutable IDs for all entities.
- IDs remain consistent across pages and document artifacts.
4. Deterministic output
- No ambiguous statuses.
- All statuses resolve to known enums.
## Core API Domains
### 1) Veteran Profile APIs
Purpose: identity anchoring and workflow gating.
- GET /api/veteran/{veteranId}
- PUT /api/veteran/{veteranId}
- GET /api/veteran/{veteranId}/readiness
Outputs:
- VeteranProfile
- ProfileReadinessSummary
### 2) Military Service APIs
Purpose: eligibility, service timelines, deployments, awards.
- GET /api/service/{veteranId}
- POST /api/service
- PUT /api/service/{serviceId}
- GET /api/service/{veteranId}/summary
- GET /api/service/{veteranId}/scanner-issues
Outputs:
- MilitaryServiceSummary
- ScannerIssue[]
### 3) Service Treatment Record APIs
Purpose: medical evidence coverage validation.
- GET /api/str/{veteranId}
- POST /api/str/upload
- GET /api/str/{veteranId}/coverage
- GET /api/str/{veteranId}/scanner-issues
Outputs:
- STRCoverageSummary
- CoverageGap[]
### 4) Current Treatment APIs
Purpose: diagnosis confirmation and nexus scoring.
- GET /api/treatment/{veteranId}
- POST /api/treatment
- PUT /api/treatment/{treatmentId}
- GET /api/treatment/{veteranId}/summary
Outputs:
- CurrentTreatmentSummary
- NexusIndicator[]
### 5) VA Rating Decision APIs
Purpose: decision history, grant/deny analysis.
- GET /api/rating/{veteranId}
- POST /api/rating
- GET /api/rating/{decisionId}
- GET /api/rating/{veteranId}/summary
- GET /api/rating/{decisionId}/denial/{conditionId}
Outputs:
- RatingDecisionSummary
- DenialRationale
### 6) Document and Artifact APIs
Purpose: source-of-truth document handling.
- POST /api/document/upload
- GET /api/document/{documentId}
- GET /api/document/{documentId}/parsed
- GET /api/document/{documentId}/references
Outputs:
- ParsedText
- EntityReference[]
### 7) Scanner and AI Analysis APIs
Purpose: cross-page validation and confidence scoring.
- POST /api/scanner/run
- GET /api/scanner/{veteranId}/issues
- GET /api/scanner/{veteranId}/confidence
- GET /api/scanner/{veteranId}/export
Outputs:
- ScannerIssue[]
- ConfidenceScore
- ScanArtifact (PDF/TXT)
### 8) Unified Readiness APIs
Purpose: workflow orchestration and gating.
- GET /api/readiness/{veteranId}
- GET /api/readiness/{veteranId}/blocking
- GET /api/readiness/{veteranId}/timeline
Outputs:
- DevelopmentReadiness
- BlockingIssue[]
### 9) Audit and Integrity APIs
Purpose: traceability and compliance.
- GET /api/audit/{entityId}
- POST /api/audit/log
- GET /api/integrity/{entityId}
Outputs:
- AuditEntry[]
- IntegrityHash
## Cross-API Data Contracts
All APIs reference:
- veteranId
- Stable entity IDs
- Shared enums
- Deterministic timestamps
No API emits UI-only semantics.
## AI Bot Consumption Guarantee
Combined API outputs enable an AI bot to:
- Scan a single PDF/TXT artifact
- Validate service eligibility
- Confirm medical evidence coverage
- Analyze rating decisions
- Explain denied conditions
- Produce a defensible readiness score
## Implementation Mapping (Current Mounted API Base Paths)
This section maps the target domain model above to currently mounted route bases in backend route manifest. It is an implementation snapshot and does not redefine the authoritative target contracts.
- Veteran Profile domain: not yet mounted under /api/veteran.
- Military Service domain: currently mounted under /api/military and /api/dd214.
- STR domain: currently mounted under /api/str and /api/strs.
- Current Treatment domain: currently mounted primarily under /api/scanner and tab-level workspace routes.
- VA Rating Decision domain: currently mounted under /api/rating and /api/scanner.
- Document and Artifact domain: currently mounted under /api/document-vault.
- Scanner and AI domain: currently mounted under /api/scanner and /api/scanner-diagnostics.
- Unified Readiness domain: currently mounted under /api/readiness-score and /api/timeline.
- Audit and Integrity domain: currently mounted under /api/audit; integrity endpoint surface under /api/integrity is not yet mounted.
## Adoption Notes
- Treat domain paths in this document as canonical target contracts.
- During migration, preserve backward compatibility aliases for existing route bases.
- Prefer additive rollout with explicit deprecation windows and audit logging.

# Scanner Active vs Legacy Ownership Map
Status keys:
- active: canonical module for new development and bug fixes
- supporting: active dependency module used by canonical scanners
- legacy-frozen: no new features; compatibility-only; do not route new flows here
This map freezes module-level ownership for scanner architecture modernization.
## Active (Canonical)
| Module | Path | Ownership | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Scanner API orchestrator | backend/api/scanner.js | scanner-platform | Canonical API boundary for scanner flows |
| DD214 deterministic scanner | backend/va_scanner/backend/shared/scanner/dd214Scanner.js | dd214-domain | Canonical DD214 extractor |
| STR deterministic scanner | backend/va_scanner/backend/shared/scanner/strDeterministicScanner.js | str-domain | Canonical STR extractor |
| Current treatment scanner | backend/va_scanner/backend/shared/scanner/currentTreatmentScanner.js | treatment-domain | Canonical current treatment extractor |
| Rating decision scanner | backend/va_scanner/engine/vaSuperScanner.js | rating-domain | Canonical rating decision extractor |
| Cross verification | backend/va_scanner/backend/shared/scanner/crossVerificationEngine.js | evidence-domain | Canonical DD214/STR verifier |
| Cross scanner fusion | backend/va_scanner/backend/shared/scanner/crossScannerFusionEngine.js | evidence-domain | Canonical fusion layer |
| Shared schema validators | backend/va_scanner/backend/shared/scanner/schemaValidators.js | scanner-platform | Canonical validation contract |
| OCR helper | backend/va_scanner/backend/shared/scanner/pdfOcrHelper.js | scanner-platform | Canonical OCR fallback |
| PDF extractor | backend/utils/pdfTextExtractor.js | scanner-platform | Canonical text-layer extraction |
| Queue | backend/va_scanner/queue/pdfQueue.js | scanner-platform | Canonical async queue |
| Queue worker | backend/va_scanner/queue/pdfWorker.js | scanner-platform | Canonical worker runtime |
| DD214 distributed cache | backend/cache/distributed-dd214-cache.js | scanner-platform | Canonical DD214 cache |
| Unified telemetry | backend/telemetry/scanner-unified-telemetry.js | scanner-platform | Canonical telemetry schema |
| DD214 field telemetry | backend/telemetry/dd214-field-telemetry.js | dd214-domain | Domain telemetry extension |
## Supporting
| Module | Path | Ownership | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| DD214 analysis orchestrator | backend/va_scanner/backend/shared/scanner/dd214Analysis/index.js | dd214-domain | Validation, evidence mapping |
| STR analysis orchestrator | backend/va_scanner/backend/shared/scanner/strAnalysis/index.js | str-domain | Timeline + cross-validation |
| Current treatment analysis orchestrator | backend/va_scanner/backend/shared/scanner/currentTreatmentAnalysis/index.js | treatment-domain | Timeline + cross-validation |
| Rating decision analysis | backend/va_scanner/backend/shared/scanner/ratingDecisionAnalysis.js | rating-domain | Structured rating analysis |
| Scanner middleware | backend/va_scanner/backend/shared/scanner/scannerMiddleware.js | scanner-platform | Normalization/meta helpers |
| Document classifier | backend/va_scanner/backend/services/scannerDocumentClassifier.js | scanner-platform | Heuristic classifier |
## Legacy-Frozen (No New Features)
No-call confirmation basis: workspace-wide reference search did not show active route imports for these modules in canonical scanner API flows.
| Module | Path | Ownership | Freeze reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| Legacy STR parser utility | backend/services/strParser.js | legacy-maintenance | Duplicates STR extraction patterns already in canonical scanner paths |
| Legacy CP exam parser utility | backend/services/cpExamParser.js | legacy-maintenance | Duplicates CP exam logic in shared scanner path |
| Legacy denial regex extractor | backend/engine/DenialReasonRegexExtractor.js | legacy-maintenance | Overlaps rating decision extraction in vaSuperScanner |
| Legacy queue implementation | backend/queue/pdfQueue.js | legacy-maintenance | Parallel queue implementation outside canonical va_scanner queue |
| Transitional scanner service | backend/va_scanner/backend/services/newScannerService.js | legacy-maintenance | Parallel service layer not used by canonical scanner API routes |
| Transitional AI scanner service | backend/va_scanner/backend/services/aiScannerService.js | legacy-maintenance | Optional enhancement path; not canonical deterministic path |
| Legacy STR controller pipeline | backend/controllers/strsController.js | legacy-maintenance | Uses legacy queue and older STR engine path |
## Ownership Freeze Policy
1. New scanner work must target active canonical modules only.
2. Supporting modules may be modified only through active module changes.
3. Legacy-frozen modules are compatibility-only and must not receive feature additions.
4. Any migration from legacy-frozen to active modules requires a route-level compatibility test.
